An S3 functional test fails in 5 of 6: it requires an empty ?key= to list, which contradicts the instruction's 'A key that ... is empty ... is refused with a client error'. A Cloudinary filename check, which the audits call borderline, fails in 4 of 6. The fair failures are a DOS multipart upload regression (2 runs) and one injected-site security miss (mimo run 3). Three of six runs (deepseek runs 1 and 3, mimo run 1) fail only on the three disputed tests.

b5.open_human_question: FAIRNESS.md (2026-10-21 05:53) ends 'NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES'. It asks to confirm two readings: (a) a leading slash on a directory may be stripped only where the adapter already strips it, while the Azure absolute form directory must be refused; (b) an empty ?key= on the S3 pages GET stays a listing request rather than an empty-key refusal. These are exactly the two tests deciding most runs. No FAIRNESS-VALIDATION.md exists and the tests were not changed later (repairs testfix/fairfix 0). The 'Required: generalize' instruction rewordings were also never applied; the instruction still contains the three sentences FAIRNESS.md asked to drop or replace.

b6.reason: I checked the upstream fix d44558e (GHSA-8MQ9-5FW2-5RM4) on GitHub. Azure upload computes resolveKey('', path.posix.join(directory, filename)), so '/etc' is refused. Cloudinary strips leading slashes and validates the filename separately with resolveKey('', filename). S3 keeps `if (req.query.key)`, so an empty key lists. All three disputed decisive tests encode upstream's exact behaviour, so a model that looks up the fix passes them. Only the injected I2 app-router listing miss (1 run) and the DOS multipart regression (a keep-working error, not a trap) would survive.

c2.note: The decisive tests sit at upstream-fixed far adapters (Azure, Cloudinary) and the reported S3 handler, and they encode upstream's exact edge choices rather than a missed site. The injected siblings (I1 batch delete, I2 app-router, I3 copy) decided only one run (mimo run 3, I2 listing).

d2.evidence: environment/injection.patch adds three whole new modules (s3 batch-delete.ts, s3 app-handlers.ts, dos copy-handler.ts) exported from each index.ts. Each one copies the adapters' own style: an authorized() 401 check, a method check with res.end(404), the findErrorMessage helper, and the mediaRoot normalisation and stripMediaRoot copied from handlers.ts. No comment points at the flaw. App-router applying mediaRoot only to listing mirrors upstream handlers.ts, which did the same. Minor tells: copy-handler and batch-delete declare `mediaRoot?: string` in their config but never read it, and no route file mounts any of the three modules. They added little difficulty: 5/6 runs fixed all three.

concerns: Fragile: one test (azure 'refuses an absolute directory') fails all 6 runs. FAIRNESS.md rated it medium-risk 'maybe'. It conflicts with the keep-working clause 'directories with leading or trailing slashes', which DOS and Cloudinary functional tests enforce on the same multipart-directory shape. Stripping leaves the blob inside the container, so it is no hole.

Live instruction/test contradiction: functional s3 'treats an empty key as a listing request' requires 200, but the instruction says 'A key that ... is empty ... is refused with a client error (a 4xx response)'. It fails 5/6 runs and zeroes their reward, so it is not a fair keep-working regression. The fair keep-working failures are the DOS multipart filename regressions (deepseek run 2, mimo run 2).
The Cloudinary 'filename walks upward' test is called borderline by the audits: collapsing 'photos/../evil.png' to 'evil.png' follows the instruction's 'collapsed, not refused' rule.
Counterfactual: drop the three disputed tests and deepseek runs 1 and 3 and mimo run 1 score 1.0. The task would then be solved 2/3 by deepseek and 1/3 by mimo, so it is not a breaker.

one_line: A media-key traversal task whose 0/3 results rest on upstream's edge rules (refuse an absolute Azure directory, let an empty S3 key list) rather than missed sites; one of those tests contradicts the instruction and the other has an open human-review flag, so it is a weak, fragile breaker.
